newsitem.title: USA: Mobil replaced 133 pct of production in 96.
newsitem.headline: Mobil replaced 133 pct of production in 96.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Monday it replaced 133 percent of its oil and natural gas production with new proved reserves in 1996.
Including asset purchases and sales, additions to proved reserves in 1996 totaled 804 million barrels of oil equivalent, while annual production was 607 million barrels, the company said.
It said proved reserves at year end were 6.810 billion barrels of oil equivalent, up 197 million barrels from a year earlier.
Mobil said its proved reserves represent about 28 percent of its total resource inventory.

This inventory of estimated oil and natural gas in the ground -- most of which has not been booked as proven reserves -- grew by over 5 billion barrels of oil equivalent last year, or the equivalent of over eight years of production, the company said.
At year end, it continued, this resource inventory of proven and unproven reserves totaled over 24 billion barrels of oil equivalent, up from 18.8 billion at the end of 1995.
Over the past three years, the company has replaced, on average, 118 percent of its proved reserves, it said.
"Our continued strong performance in reserve replacement is consistent with Mobil's goal to profitably grow production and increase shareholder value," said chief executive Lucio A. Noto.
"This is being accomplished through a program which is focused in the international area and balances exploration, reservoir management and new venture opportunities, including acquisitions."

Of the 804 million barrels oil equivalent in proven reserve additions in 1996, 282 million resulted from exploration discoveries and extensions in the Aasgard Unit in Norway, offshore Eastern Canada, Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea, Mobil said.
It said another 571 million barrels came from major acquisitions, including Ampolex and a 25 percent interest in the giant Tengiz oil field in Kazakstan.
Partially offsetting these additions was a reduction of 134 million barrels from the sale of assets in the U.S. and Canada related to ongoing restructuring initiatives, it added.
